description: A timed pulse sequencer that also directs other sequencers. Each scene is held for a length of time in seconds, and the scenes are run through in order; the same scene numbers can drive other modules

params.text: Switches the sequencing on and off
Makes the run start again from the first scene once the last one has finished
Puts the current scene's settings onto the panel
Stores the settings now on the panel as a new scene at the end
Writes the settings now on the panel over the current scene
Goes back to the first scene
Goes to the scene before the current one
Goes to the scene after the current one

inputs.text: A voltage switches the sequencing on and off
A voltage switches the looping on and off
A pulse puts the current scene's settings onto the panel
A pulse stores the settings now on the panel as a new scene at the end
A pulse writes the settings now on the panel over the current scene
A pulse goes back to the first scene
A pulse goes to the scene before the current one
A pulse goes to the scene after the current one
A pulse deletes the current scene
A voltage switches recording on and off

outputs.text: A pulse when the current scene's time has run out
A pulse when the last scene of the loop has finished
A gate while the sequencing is running

notes: nothing is sequenced until scenes are stored: set a time on the display and press ADD, once for each scene.
ADD stores a scene when recording is off, or when recording and the sequencing are both on; it does nothing while recording is on and the sequencing is off.
with recording on and the sequencing running, the time display counts up on its own, so pressing ADD stores however long the scene has lasted and starts timing the next one.
